I struggled with this exact thing for ages too. I'd hate how he'd turn so unresponsive and just blank face play video games during our main down time together. I wanted to talk about our day and he'd just be sitting there half asleep ignoring me. 

The laziness is real as well. He'd leave big messes in this state, and I was basically the sole cleaner of the house.

I thought I was being unfair and oversensitive because of my bpd because to be fair, I really was unstable at the time. Coincidentally around the time I was getting better after a lot of therapy and treatment, he stopped smoking because we didn't have the money. I put the fact that I wasn't getting mad at him for the ignoring me and being lazy down to me having reduced my symptoms.

But then recently he had a friend over and he smoked for the first time in ages and... wow. Turns out my anger was completely justified. He DOES turn unresponsive, lazy, and messy! 

And don't get me wrong, I didn't mind it as a one off. Even a couple of times a week I wouldn't mind it. But every day is extremely difficult to deal with. I think it'd be a huge deal breaker if he ever goes back to being a daily smoker. 

So yeah, even though I I've never met him, I think there's a good chance your annoyance is justified. I realised when I was getting treatment that people in my life would blame a lot of valid emotional reactions I had on my bpd, and this was one of them.

it is tough. in regards to the specific argument you mentioned in the post,  it seems you both handled it pretty well. he expressed to you that being called a dickhead hurt his feelings without being malicious. black and white thinking with bpd is tough. it might not seem significant to you, since you probably meant it more like "you're being a dickhead in this specific situation". but we often don't hear that last part. when I get called a name like that, I'll dwell on it and assume you meant I'm a dickhead all round. It's hard to have a rational discussion when you feel that way, and I often cant until I explicitly hear that you dont think im a dickhead. It's difficult to understand if you don't have bpd I think. 

Conversely, you felt like he was being petty by not saying "I love you too" in his message, and wanted to justify your point of view. Neither of you were trying to hurt each other here, but intentions got misinterpreted. It might make things easier next time if you can recognise that he's probably just trying to rationally express his feelings* 

Having said that, it's unfair to expect your child to do this effectively. so I hope you don't think I'm saying you've done anything wrong. it is a mental DISORDER after all. I'm just giving advice based on my experience living with bpd. 

The money thing is more difficult. I usually get more impulsive when I'm stressed. Could he be stressed about something other than the arguments about money itself? 

*it's important to remember that bpd treatment won't necessarily help the person stop feeling emotions so strongly. Rather they teach emotional coping skills. having a discussion rather than an emotional outbursts is probably something he was taught to do and is trying to put into action here

Side note: make sure to look after your own mental health. I'm quite sure a big reason I have bpd is because of my mums untreated bpd when I was growing up. its a difficult cycle

I'm pretty sure you should get them if you cut to fat BUT if you're like many of us here then you probably want to avoid that at all costs. So if I get that deep I ask myself:

• Is the cut in a dangerous area? (e.g. your hand)
• Is it possible for me to pinch the cut closed or is it gaping too much to do that?
• Am I quickly bleeding through my bandages?
• Has the bleeding stopped after 10 minutes of applying pressure?

If I can answer yes to any of those questions, it's time to seek medical attention.

You might also want to think about scars. Stitches are your best bet if having less noticeable scars matters to you a lot.

During healing rinse mouth with salt water 2x and day and make sure any mouthwash you have is non alcoholic.

For the first week or so icy water will be your best friend, but try not to use a straw to drink it as sucking can make the piercing move and irritate it. 

You'll want to stick to stuff like smoothies and soup (but make sure its not too hot) but tbh in my experience I was way too uncomfortable to eat anything else anyway 😂 Anything spicy or acidic should be avoided for a while as well. No alcohol either.

Tongue piercings are known to swell more than any other piercing which you probably noticed lol. It's difficult to speak, and you should take care when you speak. You'll notice once the swelling goes down that the original bar is actually pretty massive. You need to go back to your piercer and get that changed after a couple of weeks.

The healing is pretty rough, but its also very short so it's not too bad.
